divergence.title: Physical disruption underway — and priced
divergence.text: Corridor tanker flow is -69% vs its pre-war norm and Brent is +19% over 30 days at $115. The market is tracking the physical reality. Watch for the reverse divergence: flows recovering while price stays high would mean the premium is ready to bleed out.

hormuz.text: Strait of Hormuz: observed tanker flow is -98% vs its pre-war norm (1.0/day vs ~50) — either a severe physical disruption or heavy AIS signal loss (jamming/dark sailing). Cross-check the headlines.

bab_el_mandeb.text: Bab el-Mandeb Strait: observed tanker flow is -72% vs its pre-war norm (7.4/day vs ~26) — either a severe physical disruption or heavy AIS signal loss (jamming/dark sailing). Cross-check the headlines.

suez.text: Suez Canal: tanker flow is -36% vs its pre-war norm — a meaningful disruption is underway.

cape_good_hope.text: Cape of Good Hope traffic is +92% vs its pre-war norm — ships are paying 10–14 extra days to avoid the Red Sea, confirming the disruption is real.

bosporus.text: Bosporus Strait: tanker flow is -35% vs its pre-war norm — a meaningful disruption is underway.

kerch.text: Kerch Strait: observed tanker flow is -100% vs its pre-war norm (0.0/day vs ~12) — either a severe physical disruption or heavy AIS signal loss (jamming/dark sailing). Cross-check the headlines.

taiwan_strait.text: Taiwan Strait: tanker flow is -6% vs its pre-war norm — moving freely.

brent.text: Brent is $115 (+19% in 30 days, +72% in 1 year): a genuine supply-fear price — this level acts as a global tax and keeps central banks nervous.
